about: Task-force facts for scope tasks the main gap snapshot does not hold (other vector sets cover them), read by scripts/generate-complete.ts only; loadTask never reads this file (scripts/gap-snapshot.ts, rev named in tfCommit).

invalidExamples.note: Missing `bundleId`. There is no default bundle, and an absent handle must never read as 'all of my open bundles' — abort is destructive, and a fan-out is the last thing an omitted member should mean.
`bundleId` that is not a UUID. The pattern is what keeps a crafted handle from reaching the recipient's store as a lookup key.
Bare/unnamespaced ext key — SPEC §4.5.1 requires every immediate child of ext to be reverse-DNS namespaced.

Unknown top-level member — additionalProperties: false catches `force`. Abort has no forced variant: it already discards the bytes, and a member suggesting a harder version would be read as one by an implementer who has not checked.
Missing `bundleId`. There is no current bundle and no most-recent default — an absent handle must never resolve to one.
`bundleId` that is not a UUID. The pattern is what keeps a guessed or crafted handle from reaching the recipient's store as a lookup key.
Bare/unnamespaced ext key — SPEC §4.5.1 requires every immediate child of ext to be reverse-DNS namespaced.

Unknown top-level member — additionalProperties: false catches `downloaded`. Whether the bytes were fetched is the recipient's observation; a producer asserting it would be asserting a fact only the recipient holds.
Missing both `bundleId` and `password`. There is no current bundle and no recipient-held password — an absent handle must never resolve to one, on the task that replaces the node.
Missing `password`. A bundle is encrypted; there is no unpassworded path, and an absent member must not be read as one.
`bundleId` that is not a UUID. The pattern is what keeps a crafted handle from reaching the recipient's store as a lookup key.

`confirm` as the string "false". A producer intending a rehearsal would otherwise be read as truthy by a lenient consumer and get an irreversible commit — the exact substitution this member exists to prevent.
Bare/unnamespaced ext key — SPEC §4.5.1 requires every immediate child of ext to be reverse-DNS namespaced.

Unknown top-level member — additionalProperties: false catches `sourceDid`. What the bundle came from is what the recipient reads out of it and reports; a producer asserting it would be asserting the one fact the preview exists to establish.
Missing `index`. There is no 'next chunk' — the producer names what it wants, which is what makes a retry or a resume a plain repeat rather than a cursor the recipient must track.
Negative `index`. Caught by the schema rather than left to be read as 'from the end' by a lenient consumer.
`index` beyond the 4096-chunk bound. No manifest can describe it, so it never reaches a lookup.
`bundleId` that is not a UUID. The pattern keeps a crafted handle from reaching the recipient's store as a lookup key.

Unknown top-level member — additionalProperties: false catches `transportToken`. A chunked retrieval is authorized by the authenticated sender, never by a bearer token; accepting one here would invite implementations to treat it as sufficient.
Missing both pre-commitments. A slot opened without a digest accepts whatever arrives, which is exactly the property that makes a leaked write token harmless when they are present.
Uppercase hex digest. The pattern fixes one spelling so that a recipient's comparison is a string equality rather than a normalisation it might get wrong.
Digest of the wrong length — a SHA-1 in a SHA-256 member. Caught by the pattern before a slot is opened.
Zero `expectedSizeBytes`. There is nothing to import, and a slot sized for no bytes would accept an empty upload as a successful transfer.
Bare/unnamespaced ext key — SPEC §4.5.1 requires every immediate child of ext to be reverse-DNS namespaced.

Unknown top-level member — additionalProperties: false catches `password`. The password belongs to finalize-import; accepting it here would put the decryption secret alongside the slot that holds the ciphertext, which is the one place this family keeps them apart.
Chunk manifest with `chunkSize` above the 262144-byte ceiling. Every put-chunk that followed would exceed a 1 MiB mediator message and be dropped in transit, so the slot is refused before it opens.
Per-chunk digests as bare hex. Chunk digests are DigestMultibase, so the hash algorithm travels with the value; a bare hex string hard-codes one algorithm into the wire contract.
Chunk manifest with no digests. A manifest that commits to nothing lets any bytes be written at any index, which is the substitution the pre-commitment exists to prevent.
Missing `digestMultibase`. The producer restates the digest it pre-committed so that a chunk written to the wrong index is caught as a mismatch at the index, not only after reassembly.
Missing `data`. There is no empty chunk: a chunk holds at least one byte.

`data` in standard base64 with padding. The member is base64url without padding; accepting both alphabets makes the same chunk two different strings, and `+`, `/` and `=` are exactly what a lenient decoder silently drops.
Digest as bare hex. Chunk digests are DigestMultibase, so the hash algorithm travels with the value.
Unknown top-level member is rejected (additionalProperties: false).
`overrides` is required.
`overrides` must have at least one entry.
One of `credential_response` or `sealed` is required.
Both delivery paths at once is rejected — exactly one, or a consumer must guess which is authoritative.
`sealed` must be a non-empty armored string.
`credential_response` must be an object, not a string.
Unknown top-level member is rejected (additionalProperties: false).
The secret in the clear. Only a sealed bundle is accepted, so that no relay, proxy or log ever holds it.
A bundle that is not ASCII armor.
A bare digest as the fingerprint. An unkeyed hash of a secret lets anyone who reads it test guesses offline; only a SecretFingerprint, keyed at the custodian, is accepted.

payload.sealedSecret:
-----BEGIN VTA SEALED BUNDLE-----
Bundle-Id: 9f3c…
Digest-Algo: sha-256
Chunk: 0/1

U2VhbGVkU2VjcmV0Q2lwaGVydGV4dFNlYWxlZFNlY3JldENpcGhlcnRleHQ
=Q1JD
-----END VTA SEALED BUNDLE-----

invalidExamples.note: Both `scope` and `presign`. One issuance is either a session or token credential, or a batch of presigned requests, never both.
A `put` with no checksum. A write is always bound to its exact length and SHA-256, so storage refuses other bytes.
A checksum in hex. S3 takes `x-amz-checksum-sha256` in base64; a value storage cannot compare would bind nothing.
Part number 0. S3 numbers parts from 1.
An `upload-part` with no length. A part is always bound to its exact length.

65 operations, above the batch ceiling of 64. Presigned requests are bearer authority for their lifetime, so a batch is held to what a consumer can use before they expire; a larger upload asks again or uses larger parts.
An object key carrying a `/`, which would name an object outside the one the batch is bound to.
An operation outside the vocabulary. CopyObject, a bucket listing or an ACL change cannot be presigned by this task.
An upload id carrying a quote and a space, which could break out of a query parameter if interpolated rather than encoded.
A member a `get` does not take. Each operation carries exactly what its request signs.
A consumer DID in the payload. Who is asking is proven by the document, never claimed in it.
A lifetime above one hour, the family ceiling.
Presigned URLs in the clear in the response. Only the sealed bundle may carry them.

invalidExamples.note: No attributeId — the one required member. A get without a subject is a listing, and this task deliberately cannot be one.
Several identifiers. Refused by the schema rather than by a maintainer's discipline: accepting a list here would recreate the enumeration the task exists to avoid.
attributeId is not a ULID.
version 0 — versions count from 1, and 0 is the expectedVersion convention from the write tasks leaking into a read.
Unknown top-level member — additionalProperties: false catches `includeValues`, the plural from persona/attribute/list, which is the typo a builder moving between the two will actually make.
Bare, unnamespaced ext key — SPEC §4.5.1 requires every immediate child of ext to be reverse-DNS namespaced.
`contactId` is required — a get reads one contact; enumeration is persona/contact/list.

Unknown request member — additionalProperties: false catches `includeAnnotations`. Annotations are the holder's and always come back to the holder's own client; there is no switch to ask for them, and none to ask a maintainer to send them anywhere else.
Response without `starred` — an unstarred contact says `false`; absence would leave a consumer guessing.
Response with an empty `lists` — a contact on no list has no `lists` member.
Response with a list name in `lists` — it carries ListIds; a name is resolved through persona/contact/lists/show, so renaming a list touches no contact.
`listId` is required — a delete names one list; there is no delete-all.
Unknown member — additionalProperties: false catches `deleteContacts`. Deleting a list never deletes a contact; that is persona/contact/delete, one contact at a time.
Response without `existed` — a repeated delete must be distinguishable from the first.
Response echoing the list's name — additionalProperties: false; nothing deleted is echoed into logs that outlive it.
A create without `name` — a list nobody can tell apart from another is not worth creating.
An update that changes nothing — `listId` alone names a list and no change.
Colour given and removed together — dependentSchemas makes `removeColour` exclude `colour`.
`removeColour` on a create — there is no colour to remove; a create without `colour` has none.
Uppercase hex colour — one way to write each colour, lowercase.
A name with a line break — one line, so a list name cannot render as a forged second line in a picker.
Negative `order`.
Setting membership here — additionalProperties: false catches `contactIds`. A contact's lists are set on the contact with persona/contact/put 1.1, so membership has one writer.
Response without `changed` — a client could not tell an applied rename from a no-op.
Response carrying the pre-1.1 `created` flag — renamed `wasCreated`, since `created` is reserved for a timestamp; additionalProperties: false rejects the old name and `wasCreated` is required.
`listId` is required — show reads one list; enumeration is persona/contact/lists/list.
Addressing a list by name — `listId` is a ULID, so renaming a list never changes how it is addressed.
Response with a list name over 64 characters.

list.name: People I met at the spring meetup who said they would review my pull request

invalidExamples.note: Response inlining the list's contacts — additionalProperties: false catches `contacts`; members are read with persona/contact/list and `listId`.

Both forms at once — a filing names no `contactId`; the agent keys a filing on (contextId, subjectDid, knownByPersona), and a request that also named a contact would let a caller graft one peer's disclosure onto another's record.
Annotating form carrying a document — an annotation never appends a revision, so a `document` beside `contactId` has no defined meaning.
Annotating form that changes nothing — `contactId` alone names a contact and no annotation, which the anyOf over the annotation members refuses.
Neither form — a filing without `document`.
A petname given and removed in the same request — dependentSchemas makes `removePetname` exclude `petname`.
`removeLists: false` — only `true` is meaningful, so only `true` is accepted; a false remove flag would be a second way to say "unchanged".
Petname over 64 characters.

payload.petname: Sam, who I met at the climbing gym on a Thursday and who knows Dana's brother

invalidExamples.note: Petname with a line break — one line, so a surface that shows it beside a display name cannot be made to render a second, forged line.
Empty `lists` — a contact on no list has no `lists`; take it off every list with `removeLists`, so there is one way to say "none".
Repeated list identifier — `lists` is a set.
`directoryRef` without `entryId` — a link to a community and no entry would mark the contact as known through that community while naming nothing the client can join on.
`entryId` outside its pattern — it is opaque, carried exactly as the directory returned it, and never contains a separator a client might split on.
`directoryRef` with an unknown member — additionalProperties: false catches `memberDid`; the link names an entry, never the member's DID.
Response without `annotationsChanged` — a client could not tell an applied change from a no-op.
Response echoing the petname — additionalProperties: false; a response carries identifiers and flags, never annotation text that a log would then keep.

Linking with a DID as well — a request naming `subjectDid` and a document is a filing, and one naming neither is a link; one that named a DID beside a bare directory link would leave the agent to guess which contact it means.
Linking without the persona — a contact belongs to a relationship, so the agent cannot find or make the contact for an entry without the persona that knows it.
Response carrying the pre-1.2 `created` flag — renamed `wasCreated`, since `created` is reserved for a timestamp; additionalProperties: false rejects the old name and `wasCreated` is required.
Missing required request VP.
Missing required context.
Unknown top-level payload member (additionalProperties: false catches `extras`).
assertion outside the enum.
BootstrapRequest.holder is not a did:key.
BootstrapRequest.nonce wrong length (base64url-no-pad of 16 bytes is exactly 22 chars).
ask.type unknown — discriminated union rejects.
TemplateBootstrap ask missing required `template`.
AdminRotation ask missing required `adminTemplate`.
DataIntegrityProof.proofPurpose must be `authentication`.

adminScope outside the enum. `superAdmin` is the word an operator says; the wire names the shape of the ACL entry (`unrestricted` — no context list) rather than the informal name of the role that shape produces.
